<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

class AuthController extends Controller
{
    public function register(Request $request)
    {
        $validator = Validator::make($request->all(), [
            'user_name' => 'required|string|max:255',
            'email' => 'required|string|email|max:255|unique:user,email',
            'password' => 'required|string|min:8|confirmed',
        ]);

        if ($validator->fails()) {
            return response()->json([
                'message' => 'Validation failed',
                'errors' => $validator->errors(),
            ], 422);
        }

        $user = User::create([
            'user_name' => $request->input('user_name'),
            'email' => $request->input('email'),
            'user_password' => Hash::make($request->input('password')),
        ]);

        $token = auth()->login($user);

        return response()->json([
            'message' => 'User registered successfully',
            'user' => $user,
            'token' => $token,
            'token_type' => 'bearer',
            'expires_in' => auth()->factory()->getTTL() * 60,
        ], 201);
    }

    public function login(Request $request)
    {
        $validator = Validator::make($request->all(), [
            'email' => 'required|email',
            'password' => 'required|string',
        ]);

        if ($validator->fails()) {
            return response()->json([
                'message' => 'Validation failed',
                'errors' => $validator->errors(),
            ], 422);
        }

        $credentials = $request->only('email', 'password');

        if (! $token = auth()->attempt($credentials)) {
            return response()->json([
                'message' => 'Invalid credentials',
            ], 401);
        }

        return response()->json([
            'message' => 'User logged in successfully',
            'user' => auth()->user(),
            'token' => $token,
            'token_type' => 'bearer',
            'expires_in' => auth()->factory()->getTTL() * 60,
        ]);
    }

    public function me()
    {
        return response()->json(auth()->user());
    }

    public function logout()
    {
        auth()->logout();

        return response()->json([
            'message' => 'User logged out successfully',
        ]);
    }
}

Shared Hosting Deployment (Frontend built into Laravel public folder)

This project can be deployed to a shared hosting environment by publishing the React frontend build into the Laravel public directory and pointing the domain/subdomain to that folder.

### Recommended deployment layout

```text
public_html/
  agasaja-erp/
    laravel-api/
      public/
```

If the subdomain points to the Laravel public folder, the browser loads the generated `index.html` file and the built front-end assets are served correctly.

### 1. Build the frontend

From the frontend folder:

```bash
cd reactfront
npm install
npm run build
```

This generates the production files in:

```text
reactfront/dist/
```

### 2. Publish the frontend build to the Laravel public folder

Copy the contents of `reactfront/dist/` into the Laravel public directory:

```bash
cp -r reactfront/dist/* laravel-api/public/
```

If you use GitHub deployment automation, commit the built files or deploy the project in a way that copies the build output to `laravel-api/public/` before upload.

### 3. Point the subdomain to the Laravel public folder

In the hosting control panel, set the subdomain document root to the folder that contains the Laravel public directory, for example:

```text
/home/your-user/domains/your-domain.com/public_html/agasaja-erp/laravel-api/public
```

That folder is the one serving the application to the browser. If the root contains the generated `index.html`, the site loads as normal.

### 4. SPA routing on shared hosting

Because the frontend uses client-side routes, the server must serve `index.html` for unknown paths. In Apache, this is usually done with a `.htaccess` file in the public folder:

```apache
<IfModule mod_rewrite.c>
    RewriteEngine On
    RewriteBase /
    RewriteRule ^index\.html$ - [L]
    RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f
    RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-d
    RewriteRule . /index.html [L]
</IfModule>
```

### 5. GitHub deployment flow

A common GitHub + Hostinger setup is:

1. Commit the project to GitHub
2. Push to the main branch
3. In Hostinger, connect the repository and trigger a redeploy
4. Make sure the deployment copies the built frontend output to `laravel-api/public/`
5. Point the subdomain to the Laravel public folder

This way the public folder contains the generated React assets, and the browser loads the app from the root of the subdomain.

### 6. Backend configuration in production

In the Laravel backend, configure `.env` for the production database and domain:

```dotenv
APP_ENV=production
APP_DEBUG=false
APP_URL=https://your-domain.com

DB_CONNECTION=mysql
DB_HOST=127.0.0.1
DB_PORT=3306
DB_DATABASE=your_database
DB_USERNAME=your_user
DB_PASSWORD=your_password
```

Also ensure the Laravel framework tables exist in the database:

```bash
php artisan session:table
php artisan cache:table
php artisan queue:table
php artisan queue:failed-table
php artisan queue:batches-table
php artisan migrate
```

### 7. Frontend API base URL in production

Replace localhost endpoints with the production API URL, for example:

```text
https://your-domain.com/api
```

or, if using a dedicated API subdomain:

```text
https://api.your-domain.com/api
```

### 8. Final deployment checklist

- Build the React app: `npm run build`
- Copy the files into `laravel-api/public/`
- Commit and push changes to GitHub
- Redeploy from Hostinger
- Set the subdomain document root to the Laravel public folder
- Verify `index.html` loads and frontend routes render correctly
- Verify API calls are pointed to production URLs instead of `localhost`

## Likely root cause

Your Xdebug config has a few problems, and the biggest ones are:

1. You have duplicate `zend_extension` lines
   ```ini
   zend_extension=/usr/lib/php/20230831/xdebug.so
   zend_extension = xdebug
   ```
   Keep only one. This is a common reason for Xdebug to silently fail.

2. “Listen for Xdebug” does not start debugging by itself
   - In VS Code, starting the PHP listener only waits for incoming debug connections.
   - The request must actually trigger Xdebug, usually by:
     - browser extension / Xdebug helper, or
     - URL with `?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=VSCODE`, or

---

## Recommended config

```ini
[xdebug]
zend_extension=/usr/lib/php/20230831/xdebug.so
xdebug.mode=debug
xdebug.discover_client_host=0
xdebug.client_host=127.0.0.1
xdebug.client_port=9003
xdebug.idekey=VSCODE
xdebug.start_with_request=yes
xdebug.log=/var/log/xdebug.log
xdebug.log_level=7
xdebug.show_local_vars=0
```

response.value:
No — `xdebug.idekey` is not mandatory.

It is only a matching key used by Xdebug to identify which IDE should receive the debug session. It is not what makes Xdebug work. The actual essentials are:

- `xdebug.mode=debug`
- `xdebug.client_host=127.0.0.1` or `localhost`
- `xdebug.client_port=9003`
- a request that triggers Xdebug
- your VS Code PHP debugger listening on that port

So this is valid:

```ini
xdebug.idekey="netbeans-xdebug"
```

and this will also work in VS Code as long as the request triggers the same IDE key.

The important thing is consistency:
- if you set `idekey=netbeans-xdebug`, then the request must also carry that value
- usually via:
  - `?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug`
  - or a browser Xdebug helper extension configured with the same key

Example:

```text
http://localhost:8741/api/register?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug
```

If you keep `netbeans-xdebug`, then you do not need to change to `VSCODE` unless you want to match the common VS Code example.

What is often confusing is that VS Code examples commonly use:

```ini
xdebug.idekey=VSCODE
```

but that is just convention, not a requirement.

Important note:
- Your React app is not what triggers PHP Xdebug.
- The PHP breakpoint will only stop when the request reaches your Laravel PHP code on port 8741.
- The browser or an Xdebug helper must initiate that request with the debug session key.

So in your case:
- if the project previously worked with `netbeans-xdebug`, keep it
- make sure the request from the browser includes the same key
- and keep only one `zend_extension` line in php.ini

Recommended final setup:

```ini
[xdebug]
zend_extension=/usr/lib/php/20230831/xdebug.so
xdebug.mode=debug
xdebug.discover_client_host=0
xdebug.client_host=127.0.0.1
xdebug.client_port=9003
xdebug.idekey="netbeans-xdebug"
xdebug.start_with_request=yes
xdebug.log=/var/log/xdebug.log
xdebug.log_level=7
```

Then start:
- Laravel: `php artisan serve --port=8741`
- VS Code: `PHP: Listen for Xdebug`
- trigger request from browser with:
  `?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug`

If you want, I can give you the exact browser-side and VS Code-side setup for your current Laravel + React stack so it stops reliably on PHP breakpoints.

Short answer: not in the normal PHP debug config itself.

`XDEBUG_SESSION_START` is a URL parameter sent to the app request. It is not a VS Code launch setting.

What you can do in VS Code is either:

1. Use a browser extension / Xdebug helper to trigger the request
2. Open the URL directly in the browser with the query string:
   `http://localhost:8741/api/register?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug`
3. Or configure a custom launch target that starts a browser pointing to that URL

For your setup, the practical method is:

- keep VS Code listening on port `9003`
- open the browser to the Laravel URL with the query string
- the request reaches Laravel and triggers Xdebug
- PHP stops at your breakpoint

Example:

```text
http://localhost:8741/api/register?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug
```

or for a page:

```text
http://localhost:5173/?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug
```

But for PHP breakpoints in the Laravel API, the actual request must hit the PHP server, so the first URL is the relevant one.

So:
- `launch.json` can launch Firefox to `http://localhost:5173`
- but it cannot “inject” the debug cookie/session into every request automatically unless you use a browser extension or a custom script
- the standard way is still to trigger the request with `?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=...`

If you want, I can create a proper `launch.json` setup that opens Firefox to a URL like:

```text
http://localhost:8741/api/register?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug
```

so you can test the backend breakpoint directly.

response.value:
## Short answer

No — launching Firefox to `http://localhost:5173` will not trigger PHP Xdebug by itself.

Your current setup is:

- React app runs in Vite at `http://localhost:5173`
- Laravel app runs at `http://localhost:8741`

But PHP breakpoints only fire when the PHP request itself is triggered with Xdebug enabled. A React page load does not automatically initiate a PHP debug session.

---

## Why your current flow does not stop

This is the key difference:

- `PHP: Listen for Xdebug` = “wait for incoming debug connection”
- `Firefox: Vite app` = “open the frontend app”
- `http://localhost:5173` = frontend dev server, not Laravel PHP server

The browser is not hitting Laravel at `http://localhost:8741/...` with an Xdebug trigger, so the PHP request never enters debug mode.

---

## What to do instead

You need one of these:

### Option 1: Trigger Laravel directly
Open this URL in Firefox:

```text
http://localhost:8741/api/register?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug
```

or whichever Laravel route you want to debug.

This is the simplest way to hit a PHP breakpoint.

### Option 2: Use the Xdebug helper extension in Firefox
Install the Firefox Xdebug helper and set the IDE key to:

```ini
netbeans-xdebug
```

Then when you click the helper while on the page, it starts the debug session automatically.

### Option 3: Use a custom debug URL in launch.json
You can point Firefox directly at the PHP endpoint instead of the Vite app when debugging backend code:

```json
{
  "name": "Firefox: Laravel API debug",
  "type": "firefox",
  "request": "launch",
  "url": "http://localhost:8741/api/register?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug",
  "webRoot": "${workspaceFolder}/laravel-api"
}
```

This is the best match for your goal if you want to debug Laravel PHP.

---

## Important note

Your React Vite app and Laravel app are separate servers. So:

- to debug React frontend JS: use `localhost:5173`
- to debug Laravel PHP: use `localhost:8741` with `XDEBUG_SESSION_START`

They are not the same debug session.

---

## Recommended setup

Keep:

- PHP Xdebug listener on port `9003`
- Laravel `php artisan serve --port=8741`
- Vite `npm run dev`

Then, for actual PHP debugging:

1. start the PHP listener in VS Code
2. open Firefox to the Laravel endpoint with the query string
3. the request reaches PHP and Xdebug stops at the breakpoint

> This is the main reason you are not stopping: the browser is opening the frontend dev server, not the Laravel php endpoint that Xdebug is listening for.

If you want, I can give you the exact final debug config for both:
- PHP Laravel breakpoint debugging
- React frontend debugging

with a clean setup for your current project.

No — launching Firefox to `http://localhost:5173` will not trigger PHP Xdebug by itself.

Your current setup is:

- React app runs in Vite at `http://localhost:5173`
- Laravel app runs at `http://localhost:8741`

But PHP breakpoints only fire when the PHP request itself is triggered with Xdebug enabled. A React page load does not automatically initiate a PHP debug session.

---

## Why your current flow does not stop

This is the key difference:

- `PHP: Listen for Xdebug` = “wait for incoming debug connection”
- `Firefox: Vite app` = “open the frontend app”
- `http://localhost:5173` = frontend dev server, not Laravel PHP server

The browser is not hitting Laravel at `http://localhost:8741/...` with an Xdebug trigger, so the PHP request never enters debug mode.

---

## What to do instead

You need one of these:

### Option 1: Trigger Laravel directly
Open this URL in Firefox:

```text
http://localhost:8741/api/register?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug
```

or whichever Laravel route you want to debug.

This is the simplest way to hit a PHP breakpoint.

### Option 2: Use the Xdebug helper extension in Firefox
Install the Firefox Xdebug helper and set the IDE key to:

```ini
netbeans-xdebug
```

Then when you click the helper while on the page, it starts the debug session automatically.

### Option 3: Use a custom debug URL in launch.json
You can point Firefox directly at the PHP endpoint instead of the Vite app when debugging backend code:

```json
{
  "name": "Firefox: Laravel API debug",
  "type": "firefox",
  "request": "launch",
  "url": "http://localhost:8741/api/register?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug",
  "webRoot": "${workspaceFolder}/laravel-api"
}
```

This is the best match for your goal if you want to debug Laravel PHP.

---

## Important note

Your React Vite app and Laravel app are separate servers. So:

- to debug React frontend JS: use `localhost:5173`
- to debug Laravel PHP: use `localhost:8741` with `XDEBUG_SESSION_START`

They are not the same debug session.

---

## Recommended setup

Keep:

- PHP Xdebug listener on port `9003`
- Laravel `php artisan serve --port=8741`
- Vite `npm run dev`

Then, for actual PHP debugging:

1. start the PHP listener in VS Code
2. open Firefox to the Laravel endpoint with the query string
3. the request reaches PHP and Xdebug stops at the breakpoint

> This is the main reason you are not stopping: the browser is opening the frontend dev server, not the Laravel php endpoint that Xdebug is listening for.

If you want, I can give you the exact final debug config for both:
- PHP Laravel breakpoint debugging
- React frontend debugging

with a clean setup for your current project.

Use this exact content in

:

```json
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "name": "PHP: Listen for Xdebug",
      "type": "php",
      "request": "launch",
      "port": 9003,
      "pathMappings": {
        "/var/www/html/agasaja-erp/laravel-api": "${workspaceFolder}/laravel-api"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "Firefox: React app (Vite)",
      "type": "firefox",
      "request": "launch",
      "url": "http://localhost:5173/",
      "webRoot": "${workspaceFolder}/reactfront",
      "keepProfileChanges": true,
      "profile": "default",
      "reAttach": true
    },
    {
      "name": "Firefox: Laravel API debug",
      "type": "firefox",
      "request": "launch",
      "url": "http://localhost:8741/api/register?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug",
      "webRoot": "${workspaceFolder}/laravel-api",
      "keepProfileChanges": true,
      "profile": "default",
      "reAttach": true
    }
  ],
  "compounds": [
    {
      "name": "React + PHP debug",
      "configurations": [
        "PHP: Listen for Xdebug",
        "Firefox: React app (Vite)"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## How to use it

### 1) Start your servers
In two terminals:

```bash
cd /var/www/html/agasaja-erp/laravel-api
php artisan serve --port=8741
```

```bash
cd /var/www/html/agasaja-erp/reactfront
npm run dev
```

### 2) Start PHP debug listener
In VS Code:
- Run and Debug
- select `PHP: Listen for Xdebug`
- press F5

### 3) Debug React breakpoints
Use:

- `Firefox: React app (Vite)`

This opens the frontend at `http://localhost:5173` and will stop at React breakpoints.

### 4) Debug PHP breakpoints
Use:

- `Firefox: Laravel API debug`

This opens the Laravel URL with:

```text
?XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug
```

That trigger is what makes Xdebug start and stop at PHP breakpoints.

---

## Important rule

These are two different debug targets:

- React frontend: `http://localhost:5173`
- PHP backend: `http://localhost:8741/...?...XDEBUG_SESSION_START=netbeans-xdebug`

So:
- React breakpoints need the React launch config
- PHP breakpoints need the Laravel URL with the debug trigger

---

## Xdebug config to keep in php.ini

Use this exact config in your PHP setup:

```ini
[xdebug]
zend_extension=/usr/lib/php/20230831/xdebug.so
xdebug.mode=debug
xdebug.discover_client_host=0
xdebug.client_host=127.0.0.1
xdebug.client_port=9003
xdebug.idekey="netbeans-xdebug"
xdebug.start_with_request=yes
xdebug.log=/var/log/xdebug.log
xdebug.log_level=7
xdebug.show_local_vars=0
```

Do not keep both `zend_extension` lines together. Keep only one.

---

## Final note

If you want PHP breakpoints to stop reliably, the request must hit the Laravel PHP endpoint with the Xdebug trigger. Opening only the Vite page will not do it.

If you want, I can also give you a version that uses Chrome instead of Firefox, which is often a little smoother for Vite React debugging.

## Copy the whole chat session

There are a few easy ways, depending on where you are reading it:

### 1) In VS Code Chat / Copilot panel
If this is in the IDE interface:
- open the chat panel
- click the menu or overflow button in the chat header
- choose something like:
  - “Export conversation”
  - “Copy all”
  - or “Open transcript”

If you do not see that option, the next easiest method is to copy the transcript file from the VS Code session logs.

---

### 2) From the session transcript file
Your transcript is stored here in this environment:

```text
/home/leonardo/.config/Code/User/workspaceStorage/92dfa575f41eaaac68f4b9a8cd45913f/GitHub.copilot-chat/transcripts/b14cd978-d429-40b8-8d9b-2e2ee2eae7f6.jsonl
```

You can:
- open it in VS Code
- select all content
- copy it
- paste into a text editor or file

This is the full raw session log.

---

### 3) If you want it as a plain text file
Open the transcript file and save as:
- `.txt`
- `.md`
- or any document you want

If you want a cleaner version, you can also paste it into a new file and remove JSON formatting if needed.

---

### 4) If you are in the browser UI
Use:
- Ctrl/Cmd + A
- Ctrl/Cmd + C

to copy the visible chat content from the page, then paste it elsewhere.

---

## If you want the cleanest result
The best option is usually:
- open the transcript file
- copy all text
- paste it into a text editor
- save it as a plain text or markdown file

If you want, I can also show you a very quick way to export only the relevant conversation in a readable format.
